name: Per Trads Ørskov
story_summary: Clinical psychologist and postdoctoral researcher Per Trads Ørskov at the Center for Digital Psychiatry, Region of Southern Denmark (University of Southern Denmark), led a three-arm randomized controlled trial published in Frontiers in Virtual Reality (2025) testing virtual reality exposure therapy for social anxiety disorder. His team recorded 360° VR video of real social scenarios — restaurants, public spaces, social gatherings — using an Insta360 InstaOneX camera, edited in Unity 3D, and displayed via HTC VIVE Pro headsets. The completed RCT found that CBT augmented with VR exposure (CBT-ExpVR) delivered comparable clinical outcomes to standard CBT, with lower dropout (16% vs 38%) and reported by therapists as less costly and requiring less effort to deliver.
why_it_matters: A consumer Insta360 camera passed the bar for clinical-grade exposure therapy content in a peer-reviewed RCT. This positions Insta360 as a tool for mental health practitioners seeking affordable solutions for VR therapy — a rapidly growing market across Europe and beyond.
source_quote: The 360° videos were recorded using Insta360-InstaOneX and edited using the game engine Unity 3D.
source_type: peer-reviewed academic journal (Frontiers in Virtual Reality, Volume 6, 2025)
verification_note: Insta360 InstaOneX explicitly named in search snippets from University of Southern Denmark research portal, Frontiers, and PMC. Paper published 2025. Source returns 403 on WebFetch (bot-detection, consistent with all Frontiers papers in this dataset). Not on exclusion list. Not in previous results. Camera model older (ONE X, 2018, discontinued) — flag for human reviewer to verify quote. Authors: Ørskov P.T., Runge E., Sainte-Marie T.T.H., Ernst M.T., Clemmensen L., Dalsgaard C.H., Lichtenstein M.B., Bouchard S. Institutions: Center for Digital Psychiatry, Southern Denmark; University of Southern Denmark; Université du Québec en Outaouais, Canada.

name: Tatsuya Tanaka
story_summary: Neurosurgeon Tatsuya Tanaka at the International University of Health and Welfare (IUHW) Narita Hospital led a study installing Insta360 Pro cameras in the hospital's emergency department, operating room, and angiography suite to create 360° VR educational content for fifth-year medical students. The program gave students immersive exposure to real neurosurgery environments without requiring OR access. In a study of 85 medical students over April 2024 to March 2025, 52 students (61%) reported increased interest in neurosurgery after the VR experience, versus just 22 (26%) before. Published in the open-access journal Cureus on April 21, 2025.
why_it_matters: A neurosurgeon at a Japanese hospital used Insta360 Pro cameras to nearly triple medical student interest in neurosurgery (26% to 61%). This is a compelling case for Insta360 in hospital education departments — an institutional market Insta360 has not yet featured.

name: Cui Y et al. — Beijing Bo'ai Hospital
story_summary: Researchers at Beijing Bo'ai Hospital (China Rehabilitation Research Center) and Capital Medical University — Cui Y, Cong F, Zeng M, and Wang J — published a protocol in Frontiers in Neurology (April 2025) for a randomized controlled trial testing synchronous 360° VR video action observation (VRAO) combined with neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) for stroke rehabilitation. The team used an Insta360 ONE X2 camera to film first-person and third-person 360° VR clips of arm exercises for stroke patients to observe and imitate while receiving electrical stimulation — designed to activate mirror neurons and restore upper limb motor function. NOTE: This is a study protocol; trial results are pending.
why_it_matters: China's national rehabilitation research center is using an Insta360 ONE X2 to create therapeutic content aimed at helping stroke patients relearn arm movement. If the RCT succeeds, Insta360 footage could be directly responsible for improving quality of life for stroke survivors — a massive global health challenge.
source_quote: The first-person and third-person point of view 360° VR video clips of actions and landscapes will be shot using an Insta360 one X2 camera, and edited by Insta360 studio v5.2.4 (Insta360 Inc., Shenzhen, China).
